title: Hindiba Salatassi
description: Prepared with endive, juice, and olive oil.

ingredients.name: two or three heads of endive
ingredients.sourceText: two or three heads of endive

ingredients.name: one or two pinches of pepper
ingredients.sourceText: one or two pinches of pepper

steps: Remove the dark green leaves from endive
Pick off the others one by one
Cut the large ones in two
Wash and drain them in a cloth, by shaking it to and fro violently, and extract all the water
Put in the salad-bowl a small teaspoonful of salt, one or two pinches of pepper, the juice of a small lemon, three tablespoonfuls of olive oil
Beat up until it becomes like cream
Put in the salad
Turn it with spoon and fork till well mixed
Serve

title: Ichi Dblmush Kiizu Kebabi
description: Prepared with lamb, liver, and heart.
steps: Get the whole of a small lamb with the liver and the heart
Place it in a large saucepan or iron pot without the liver and the heart
Cover it with water, set it on the fire, and let it boil for ten or fifteen minutes
Chop up the liver very fine together with the heart
Put three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter in a stewpan with three or four chopped onions
Put it on the fire, and let them stew till nearly brown
Add the liver and the heart, with a handful of skinned pistachios, and the same of currants well cleaned
Stir till the liver begins to cook, then add two or three pounds of the best rice, well washed, sufficient salt, pepper, and cinnamon
Keep stirring, and add now and then a little of the liquor in which the lamb is boiled, until the rice is rather soft
Stuff the lamb with this preparation, and sew it up
Rub the lamb all over with some onion-juice
Place it in a baking tin, and bake it a nice brown on both sides in a very hot oven
When done, dish up, and serve

title: Imam-Bayildi
description: Prepared with onions, olive oil or butter, and egg.

ingredients.name: half a dozen peeled cloves of garlic
ingredients.sourceText: half a dozen peeled cloves of garlic

steps: Procure half a dozen egg-plants and cut each one in four lengthways without separating from the stalk
Sprinkle them with salt and let them remain for five or ten minutes
Peel and cut five or six onions in rather thick slices
Fry them partly brown in olive oil or fresh butter
Lay half of them on the bottom of a stewpan, over which place the egg-plants and lay the other half of the onions over them
Add half a dozen peeled cloves of garlic and a pint of water or little more
Put the pan on the fire and let it simmer till the egg-plants are soft
Dish them up carefully and serve hot or cold

title: Inja-Burek
description: Prepared with starch, mutton, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: a pound and a half of flour
ingredients.sourceText: a pound and a half of flour

steps: Put a pound and a half of flour on a slab, make a hole in the centre, in which put a teaspoonful of salt and four eggs
Mix all together, then add sufficient water, and form it a softish flexible paste
Dip your hands into melted fresh butter, and work it for a few minutes longer

Divide it into thirty pieces the size of walnuts, sprinkle a little wheat-starch both under and over them, and roll them out one by one with a rolling-pin as thin as a wafer, or thinner than that if you can, and the size of the baking-tin you intend to lay them in

Butter the baking-tin, in which lay five of the pieces of paste one over the other, sprinkle a little fresh butter all over, and lay five more pieces over, butter again, and over which lay five more pieces, butter again

Lay all over either minced mutton, mixed with mushrooms and onions, both chopped very fine, and previously stewed a nice brown in fresh butter, together with the meat, or cheese, or any other ingredients you may fancy
Cover it with the remaining pieces of paste in the same way as before
Cut it in four crossways, pour a little hot fresh butter over, and bake it a nice brown in a moderate oven
When done, dish up and serve

title: Injik Elmassiyessi
description: Prepared with calf's feet, powdered sugar, and juice.

ingredients.name: six or seven pints of water
ingredients.sourceText: six or seven pints of water

ingredients.name: a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar

ingredients.name: a pint and three-quarters of water
ingredients.sourceText: a pint and three-quarters of water

ingredients.name: the juice of three or four lemons
ingredients.sourceText: the juice of three or four lemons

ingredients.name: the rind of one lemon, with the pith taken off
ingredients.sourceText: the rind of one lemon, with the pith taken off

ingredients.name: the whites and shells of five or six eggs
ingredients.sourceText: the whites and shells of five or six eggs

ingredients.name: a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower

ingredients.name: a few white and black grapes
ingredients.sourceText: a few white and black grapes

steps: Procure three or four calf's feet, wash and place them in a stew-pan, with six or seven pints of water, and put it on the fire
When boiling, skim and simmer until the flesh comes off the bones; then pass it through a clean cloth or a sieve into a basin, and let it remain until quite hard
Remove all the fat, &c., from the top

Put in a saucepan a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar, a pint and three-quarters of water, the juice of three or four lemons, the rind of one, with the pith taken off, the whites and shells of five or six eggs, and stir with a wooden spoon until the sugar is dissolved
Add the jelly, set it on the fire, and stir well until it boils; then pass it through a jelly-bag till quite clear
Add a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower, and then put it in a mould, with a few white and black grapes, the same of strawberries and cherries, &c.
Place it on ice till quite firm, turn it out, and serve

title: Injir Khdshabi
description: Prepared with figs, orange, and ice.

ingredients.name: one or two pounds of figs
ingredients.sourceText: one or two pounds of figs

ingredients.name: two or three pints of hot or cold water
ingredients.sourceText: two or three pints of hot or cold water

steps: Cut off the stalks of one or two pounds of figs
Prick each one here and there with a wooden needle
Place them in a basin with two or three pints of hot or cold water
Let them remain for ten or twelve hours
Pass the liquid through a sieve into a glass bowl
Add the figs with a few drops of orange-flower and a few pieces of ice
Serve

steps: Set on the fire a stewpan, with three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter
When hot, add gradually a pound and six ounces of sago, with {{source-2}}, and keep stirring it until the almonds are a nice brown
Then pour in all at once a pint and a half of boiling milk, with boiling syrup, which you have previously made of a pound and a half of loaf sugar and a pint and a half of water
Stir it well, put the cover over, and let it remain for fifteen minutes
Then sprinkle a little rose-water over, dish up, shake some sugar over, and serve

Put it into a stewpan with two pints of water, sufficient salt

description: Prepared with rice, almonds, and syrup.

ingredients.name: a pound and a half of rice-flour

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pound of almonds, skinned and well pounded

steps: Put on the fire a stewpan with a pound of fresh butter
When melted, add gradually a pound and a half of rice-flour, with three-quarters of a pound of almonds, skinned and well pounded, and keep stirring until it becomes a gold colour
Then immediately add a pint of boiling milk, with two pints of boiling syrup, which you have previously prepared of loaf sugar and water, as in No. 159
Instantly put the cover over, and let it remain for five minutes
Then stir it well with a fork, dish it up in moulds the size of a small teacup, letting it bear the impression of the mould, and serve with some white sugar sifted over

steps: Open as many oysters as are wanted, take them out of the shells, and put them in a basin
Put three or four table spoonfuls of olive oil in a saucepan, set it on the fire

title: Jigher Kidbabi
description: Prepared with lamb or liver, fat, and wine.

ingredients.name: two or three skinned cloves of garlic
ingredients.sourceText: two or three skinned cloves of garlic

ingredients.name: half a teacup of wine vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: half a teacup of wine vinegar

steps: Cut as much as is wanted, sheep's or lamb's liver in dice, an inch and a half square
Pass them on skewers, and wrap each one with a thin piece of caul-fat
Place them before a moderate fire, and turn them slowly until the liver is nicely roasted
When done, dish it up
Well pound two or three skinned cloves of garlic in a mortar, add half a teacup of wine vinegar, two of broth, and a little salt and pepper
Stir it well with a wooden spoon, and pour it over the liver
Put the cover on the dish, and place it in the oven, or on a charcoal fire covered with ash for five minutes or so, and then serve

title: Jizleme
description: Prepared with yeast, clotted cream, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: the best flour
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of the best flour

ingredients.name: a very small piece of German yeast
ingredients.sourceText: a very small piece of German yeast

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pound of sugar
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pound of sugar

steps: Put in a basin or pan a pound of the best flour, half a teaspoonful of salt, and a very small piece of German yeast, which mix with water to form a nice crumpet dough.
Keep it covered in a warm place until it has nicely risen.
Pour a portion of it on a stove sufficient to bake a crumpet the size of a dinner plate, and as thick as a crown-piece.
When you have baked five or six, lay them in a rather deep and circular baking-tin, one over the other, and between each one a thin layer of clotted cream and powdered sugar over.
Dissolve in a saucepan three-quarters of a pound of sugar with a pint of water, add {{source-8}}, set it on the fire, and commence stirring until the butter is melted.
Pour it over the crumpets, and put the baking-tin on a very slow charcoal fire, or in the oven, for ten or fifteen minutes.
Dish it up carefully, sprinkle a little rose water over, and serve.

title: Kabak-Basstissi
description: Prepared with mutton or lamb, onions, and juice.

ingredients.name: mutton or lamb
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds of mutton or lamb

ingredients.name: juice of one or two lemons
ingredients.sourceText: juice of one or two lemons

steps: Cut {{source-0}} in pieces about the size of walnuts
Put them in a stewpan with a little salt, and cover them with water
Set it on a charcoal fire
When beginning to scum, skim it well, and let it simmer till the meat is nearly tender
Put three or four sliced onions in a fryingpan with sufficient fresh butter, and fry them partly brown
Peel four or five vegetable marrows, cut each one in four crossways, take out the insides, if seeded, and slice them three-quarters of an inch thick

Lay some of the pieces of meat on the bottom of the stewpan; then add some slices of vegetable marrow, with part of the fried onions, then meat, then pieces of vegetable marrow and onions, then meat, &c., until the whole of them are laid
Add the liquor in which the pieces of mutton were boiled, and sufficient salt; if the liquor is not enough, add some of the broth
Set the stewpan on the fire, and let it simmer until the vegetable marrow is tender
Add the juice of one or two lemons, with a little chopped mint
Let it simmer for two minutes longer, and then take it off
Dish it up, sprinkle a little pepper or cinnamon over, and serve hot

description: Prepared with leg of mutton, onions, and rice.

Dish up tastefully and serve hot

title: Kaiyssi Khdshabi
description: Prepared with apricots, powdered sugar, and essence of almonds.

ingredients.name: a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar

ingredients.name: two or three pints of water
ingredients.sourceText: two or three pints of water

ingredients.name: a few drops of the essence of almonds or other essence
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of the essence of almonds or other essence

steps: Pick out the large apricots and put the small ones in a saucepan, with half a pint of water or a little more
Set it to boil until the stones come out
Pass them through a cloth into a basin, and well squeeze the juice from them
Put the juice in the pan with a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar
Set it to boil for a minute, and pass it again through the cloth into the basin
Put the large ones in a saucepan, with two or three pints of water, and boil them until they begin to crack
Take it off and let it cool
Pass the liquor through a sieve into a glass bowl
According to taste, sweeten it with the syrup which you have prepared
Add the apricots, with a few drops of the essence of almonds or any other essence you fancy, and a few pieces of ice, and serve

description: Prepared with turbot, lemons, and oil or butter.

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pint of salt water
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pint of salt water

steps: Get a turbot as large as is required, cut the fins off, wash and sprinkle it with sufficient salt.
Cut in slices five or six lemons, lay half of them on the bottom of a convenient dish, place the fish over, and cover it with the other half of the lemons.
Pour on it three-quarters of a pint of salt water coloured with half an ounce of saffron.
Place a plate or dish over, so as to press the fish slightly, and let it remain for one night.
The next day fry it a nice brown either in oil or fresh butter, and serve.

title: Kapali Bureghi
description: Prepared with lamb or mutton, onions, and almonds.
steps: Roll out as thin as a wafer twenty pieces of paste prepared with fresh butter and eggs
Well butter the inside of a shallow and dome-like mould
Lay carefully ten of the pastes one over the other, which must reach up the brim of the mould
Place in a rather deep fryingpan some finely-minced raw lamb or mutton, two or three onions chopped fine, a little salt and a little fresh butter
Set it on the fire, and stew them partly brown
Add one or two ounces of almonds skinned, the same of pistachios, a little pepper and cinnamon
Mix them well together with a wooden spoon
Fill up the mould with this mixture
Cover the top with the remaining ten pieces of paste
Butter the bottom of a baking-tin, in which place the mould upside down
Put it in a hot oven, and bake it a nice brown
When done, turn it out of the mould on to a dish, and serve

steps: Put in a stewpan three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter, and set it on the fire
When melted, mix in by degrees about two pounds and three-quarters of the best flour, and keep stirring until the flour is partly browned
Take it out, and place it on a pastry slab, make a hole in the centre, in which put a teaspoonful of salt
Mix it with water (in which a teaspoonful of carbonate of soda is dissolved previously) into a softish paste with your hands
Form it into small cakes, and make a dent in the centre of each one with the point of your finger
Place them in a buttered tin, and bake them a nice colour
Have ready some syrup as in No. 135
When the cakes are nicely done, pour it over
Put it again in the oven, or on a slow charcoal fire until the syrup is absorbed
Dish up tastefully, and serve

steps: Pick out the large apricots and put the small ones in a saucepan with half a pint of water or a little more
Set it to boil until the stones come out
Pass them through a cloth into a basin and well squeeze the juice from them
Put the juice in the pan with a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar
Set it to boil for a minute and pass it again through the cloth into the basin
Put the large apricots in a saucepan with two or three pints of water and boil them until they begin to crack
Take it off and let it cool
Pass the liquor through a sieve into a glass bowl
Sweeten it with the syrup which you have prepared, according to taste
Add the apricots, with a few drops of the essence of almonds or any other essence you fancy, and a few pieces of ice
Serve

title: Kdymctkli Kaddyif
description: Prepared with vermicelli, clotted cream, and syrup.
steps: Prepare four pounds of vermicelli as No. 149
Lay half of it in a buttered baking-tin, and the other half in another buttered tin
Pour in each about half a pound of scalded fresh butter
Bake them a delicate colour on both sides
When cooked, strain and wash out all the butter from both
Lay some clotted cream over one, half an inch thick
Cover it with the other one
Pour hot syrup all over as No. 149
Put it again in the oven until the syrup is nearly absorbed
Cut it in any shape you fancy, or turn it on to a dish as it is, and serve

title: Kebab Kyufte
description: Pan-fried minced-meat patties with onion, parsley, bread and cinnamon. They are served hot with a lemon-flavored brown gravy or a topping of sliced onion and parsley.

ingredients.name: two or three pounds of raw leg of mutton, or beef, or veal
ingredients.sourceText: two or three pounds of raw leg of mutton, or beef, or veal

ingredients.name: half a handful of parsley cleaned

ingredients.name: crumb of a French penny roll

ingredients.name: two or three teacups of brown gravy
ingredients.sourceText: two or three teacups of brown gravy

ingredients.name: two or three teaspoonfuls of flour
ingredients.sourceText: two or three teaspoonfuls of flour

steps: Put on a chopping board two or three pounds of either a raw leg of mutton, or beef, or veal, half a handful of parsley cleaned, two or three onions peeled, and the crumb of a French penny roll
Sprinkle a little salt, pepper, and cinnamon over, and mince them very fine together until like a paste
Make it up in shapes of small buns, or any shape you may fancy, and fry them a nice colour in fresh butter
Put two or three teacups of brown gravy in a saucepan, with two or three teaspoonfuls of flour, the juice of a lemon, and a little salt
Set it on a slow fire, and keep stirring until it is a nice consistency
Dish the meat up tastefully, and pour the gravy over, and serve hot, or serve it with finely sliced onions and chopped parsley over, instead of gravy, if approved of

title: Kefal-Balighi Pulakissi
description: Prepared with olive oil, onions, and juice.

ingredients.name: half a dozen very fresh grey mullets
ingredients.sourceText: half a dozen very fresh grey mullets

ingredients.name: half a teacup of olive oil
ingredients.sourceText: half a teacup of olive oil

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pound of sliced onions
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pound of sliced onions

ingredients.name: the juice of one or two lemons
ingredients.sourceText: the juice of one or two lemons

steps: Take out the gills and the insides of half a dozen very fresh grey mullets
Cut them in two crossways
Wash and sprinkle them with a little salt and let them remain for an hour
Put in a stewpan an ounce of fresh butter and half a teacup of olive oil
Add a little salt and three-quarters of a pound of sliced onions
Put it on the fire and let the onions stew but not brown
Lay the fish over and cover it with water
Let simmer for twenty or thirty minutes
When nearly done, add a handful of chopped parsley and a pinch or two of cayenne pepper
Add the juice of one or two lemons and let it simmer for four or five minutes longer
Dish it up and serve hot

title: Khiyar Tereturu
description: Prepared with nuts or almonds, wine or vinegar or juice or lemons, and cucumbers.

ingredients.name: three or four cloves of garlic
ingredients.sourceText: three or four cloves of garlic

ingredients.name: crumb of half of a French penny roll
ingredients.sourceText: crumb of half of a French penny roll

ingredients.name: half a teacup of the best wine vinegar or juice of two or three lemons
ingredients.sourceText: half a teacup of the best wine vinegar or juice of two or three lemons

ingredients.name: one or two tablespoonfuls of the best olive oil
ingredients.sourceText: one or two tablespoonfuls of the best olive oil

steps: Crack a pound of nuts or almonds, scald and skin them, then pound them in a stone mortar
Add half a teaspoonful of salt, three or four cloves of garlic peeled, and pound them well together with the nuts
Add the crumb of half of a French penny roll, previously soaked in water, and pound again all together till it forms a smooth substance like paste
Moisten it with half a teacup of the best wine vinegar, or the juice of two or three lemons, and bring it to the consistency of cream with some water, stirring it all the time with a wooden spoon
Peel and cut in thin slices one or two cucumbers in a dish, season with a little salt and white pepper
Pour the sauce over, then pour one or two tablespoonfuls of the best olive oil over by degrees, and serve

description: Prepared with cucumbers, salt, and fennel.

ingredients.name: one or two dozen of small cucumbers
ingredients.sourceText: one or two dozen of small cucumbers

steps: Get one or two dozen of small cucumbers
Put some fennel on the bottom of a stone jar
Place the cucumbers over
Lay some fennel on the top
Cover them with salt water
Place a piece of board over them
Put an iron weight or a heavy stone on the top to press it
Put the jar for a few days in a place where the sun is powerful, or in a warm place
Remove it to a cool place
Let it remain eight or ten days before using

title: Khunkyar Pilaví
description: Prepared with rice, mutton, and pistachios.

ingredients.name: the best rice
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds of the best rice

ingredients.name: two pounds and a half of the choice part of mutton
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds and a half of the choice part of mutton

ingredients.name: half a pound of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of fresh butter

ingredients.name: three or four tablespoonfuls of pistachios
ingredients.sourceText: three or four tablespoonfuls of pistachios

ingredients.name: one or two tablespoonfuls of currants
ingredients.sourceText: one or two tablespoonfuls of currants

ingredients.name: half a teaspoonful of mixed spice
ingredients.sourceText: half a teaspoonful of mixed spice

steps: Wash {{source-0}}, put it in a clean cloth, tie it, and hang it up
Cut two pounds and a half of the choice part of mutton in pieces about the size of walnuts, wash and place them in a stewpan with four pints of water, and put it on a charcoal fire
When boiling, skim it well, add sufficient salt, and let it simmer for twenty or thirty minutes
Drain the liquor into a basin, put half a pound of fresh butter over the pieces of meat, and fry them a nice brown

Add three pints of the liquor, with a little salt, three or four tablespoonfuls of pistachios, the same of minced raw mutton, previously fried a nice colour in fresh butter, one or two of currants, and half a teaspoonful of mixed spice
As soon as it boils, add the rice, and boil it for two or three minutes longer
Reduce the heat of the fire by removing the burning coals, and leaving only the ashes and the sparks, put on the pan with the cover over for about an hour
Dish up tastefully, and serve

title: Khurma
description: Prepared with honey or sugar or water, flour, and salt.

ingredients.name: a pound and a quarter of the best flour
ingredients.sourceText: a pound and a quarter of the best flour

ingredients.name: four or five ounces of fresh butter, melted
ingredients.sourceText: four or five ounces of fresh butter, melted

ingredients.name: honey or loaf sugar and water
ingredients.sourceText: honey or loaf sugar and water

steps: Put a pound and a quarter of the best flour on the pastry-slab, make a hole in the centre, in which put a teaspoonful of salt, four or five ounces of fresh butter, melted
Mix all together, then add half a pint of water, or a little more, mixed with a little carbonate of soda, and form it a softish flexible paste
Then roll it with hands as long as it will extend, a little thicker than your thumb, and cut it up in pieces the size of a date
Then roll them one by one upon a basket-lid, or a table-mat made of fine twigs, and fry them a delicate colour in boiling fresh butter
When done, let them drain, then throw them in boiling syrup, which you have previously prepared of honey, or loaf sugar and water, and let them remain for a few minutes
Then dish them up tastefully, and serve

description: Prepared with olive oil, juice, and salt.

ingredients.name: four or five pounds of swordfish
ingredients.sourceText: four or five pounds of swordfish

ingredients.name: one or two handfuls of picked parsley
ingredients.sourceText: one or two handfuls of picked parsley

ingredients.name: five or six cloves of garlic
ingredients.sourceText: five or six cloves of garlic

ingredients.name: the juice of two or three lemons
ingredients.sourceText: the juice of two or three lemons

steps: Procure four or five pounds of swordfish in one piece
Cut it in slices, wash them, and sprinkle a little salt over
Dip them in flour and then in egg
Partly fry them in olive oil
Spread one or two handfuls of picked parsley on the bottom of a stewpan with five or six cloves of garlic
Lay the slices of fish over
Spread the same quantity of parsley and garlic on the top
Add sufficient salt and two or three pinches of Cayenne pepper
Add the juice of two or three lemons and two teacups of water
Put the pan over a charcoal fire with the lid on and let it simmer gently for twenty minutes or until the liquor is nearly absorbed
Dish it up and serve

When done, turn it on to a dish carefully, and serve

Put three chopped onions in a stewpan with some fresh butter, and partly fry them

Dish up tastefully, and serve

title: Kol-Bureghi
description: Prepared with broth, eggs, and butter.
steps: Lay on the paste-board separately as many pieces of paste as are required
Beat up two or three eggs in a basin, with three or four tablespoonfuls of broth
Dip a paste brush in it, rub it all over each piece of the paste, and fold them separately in two
Lay on each one lengthways any preparation you fancy, fold the two side edges over, and then the ends, thus making it an oblong shape
Make the others in the same shape, and fry them a nice brown on both sides in hot fresh butter
When all done, let them drain, then dish up on a white napkin, and serve hot

steps: Procure a musk-melon, or any other one
Cut out the part where the stalk is, twice the size of a crown piece, so as to form a lid
Take out the seeds, and part of the inside
Fry a nice brown a sufficient quantity of raw minced mutton in fresh butter, with two onions chopped fine
Add half a teacup of rice well cleaned, sufficient salt and pepper, a tablespoonful of currants, two or three tablespoonfuls of almonds, skinned, and the same of pistachios
Stir three or four minutes longer, and take it off
Stuff the melon with this mixture
Put the piece over that you have previously cut out for a lid, and pin it round with a few wooden pins
Put it in a baking-dish, and bake it nicely in the oven
Dish it up, and serve

title: Kuru Silkme
description: Prepared with mutton, salt, and pepper.

ingredients.name: three or four pounds of mutton
ingredients.sourceText: three or four pounds of mutton

ingredients.name: three or four ounces of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: three or four ounces of fresh butter

steps: Cut three or four pounds of mutton into small pieces, wash and dry them in a cloth, then place them in a stewpan with sufficient salt and pepper
Set it on the fire, and stir with a wooden spoon until it begins to hiss, which indicates that all the moisture is dispersed
Add three or four ounces of fresh butter, and keep stirring till the meat is nicely browned
When done, take them out with a hand-strainer, and place them in a dish; keep it hot
Cut three or four egg-plants in thin slices, sprinkle them with salt, and let them remain for a few minutes

When the bitter juice is drawn from them, fry them a nice colour on both sides in the remaining fat from the meat, then arrange them tastefully over the meat, or round the dish, sprinkle a little pepper over, and serve hot

title: Kuzu Kizdrtmassi
description: Prepared with lamb, curd, and onions.

ingredients.name: leg or any other part of lamb
ingredients.sourceText: leg or any other part of lamb

steps: Cut as much as is wanted of a leg or any other part of lamb in pieces the size of kidneys
Dip each piece in curd, and fry them a nice brown in fresh butter
Place them in a stewpan with two or three sliced onions fried in butter, sufficient salt and pepper
Cover them with hot or cold water, set it on a charcoal fire, and let it simmer gently until it forms a nice thick gravy at the bottom of the stewpan
While the meat is cooking, chop up the liver and the heart of a lamb together, then fry it in fresh butter with a little salt
When nicely done, add a handful of pistachios skinned, a tablespoonful of currants, and a little mixed spice
Stir it with a wooden spoon for five minutes or so
Place it in a saucepan, with some of the gravy of the lamb, and two pints of broth
Set it on a charcoal fire with the cover over
When boiling, add a pound of rice well washed, stir it, put the cover over, and let it boil until each grain is rather soft, but separate
Take it off, wrap round the lid a wet cloth, to prevent the steam from escaping, and put it by the side of the fire for twenty minutes or so
Dish it up in the form of a dome, arrange the pieces of lamb over tastefully, and serve hot

title: Kâlkân-Bâlighi Tâvâssi
description: Prepared with turbot, lemons, and oil or butter.
steps: Get a turbot as large as is required, cut the fins off, wash and sprinkle it with sufficient salt
Cut in slices five or six lemons, lay half of them on the bottom of a convenient dish
Place the fish over, and cover it with the other half of the lemons
Pour on it three-quarters of a pint of salt water coloured with half an ounce of saffron
Place a plate or dish over, so as to press the fish slightly, and let it remain for one night
The next day fry it a nice brown either in oil or fresh butter, and serve

title: Lharana Turshussu
description: Prepared with heart and yeast.

ingredients.sourceText: three or four nice white-heart cabbages

ingredients.name: half a dozen of ripe capsicums

steps: Cut the stalks off
Remove the outer leaves of three or four nice white-heart cabbages
Cut them in four crosswise
Put a little yeast on the bottom of a convenient stone jar
Place the cabbages over
Add half a dozen of ripe capsicums, chopped fine
Cover them with brine
Put the lid over the jar
Place it in the pantry
Pour the brine in the jar to and fro every five days
When the cabbage is turned acid, it is then fit for use

title: Limdn Elmetsiyyessi
description: Prepared with isinglass, lemons, and wine.

ingredients.name: half a pound of loaf sugar
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of loaf sugar

steps: Dissolve about an ounce of isinglass in a small tumbler of water.
Boil and reduce it to half, then pass it through a cloth into a basin.
Cut in two five lemons, take off the rind of one of them and remove the pith, place them in a basin, and squeeze the juice of the lemons into it.
Put half a pound of loaf sugar in a stewpan with a pint of water, set it to boil until it becomes a syrup.
Take it off and add the juice and the rind of the lemons.
Put the stewpan again on the fire with the cover over.
As soon as it begins to boil, skim it well, and add three wine-glasses of water by degrees.
Let it boil one or two minutes longer, then add the isinglass.
Pass it through a jelly-bag, if fancied, add two tablespoonfuls of rose-water.
Pour it into a mould, and place it on ice.
When ready, dip the mould in warm water and turn it out.
If summer, add a little more isinglass.

description: Prepared with spinach, puff-paste, and cheese.

ingredients.name: four or five very thin round pieces of puff-paste
ingredients.sourceText: four or five very thin round pieces of puff-paste

ingredients.name: half a pound of nice cheese, grated

steps: Well clean a sufficient quantity of spinach, pick off the stalks, boil it for one or two minutes, let it drain, and chop it up very fine
Well butter a rather deep and circular baking-tin, in which lay four or five very thin round pieces of puff-paste, one over the other
Sprinkle a little fresh butter over with a paste-brush, and lay the spinach all over
Break into a basin three or four eggs, to which add half a pound of nice cheese, grated; beat up well together, and lay it over the spinach
Put it in a rather hot oven, and bake it a nice colour
When done, cut it in four crossways, and serve hot

Well butter a rather deep and circular baking-tin, in which lay four or five very thin round pieces of puff-paste, one over the other
Sprinkle a little fresh butter over with a paste-brush, and lay the spinach all over
Break into a basin three or four eggs, to which add half a pound of nice cheese, grated; beat up well together, and lay it over the spinach
Put it in a rather hot oven, and bake it a nice colour
When done, cut it in four crossways, and serve hot

title: Marul Salatassi
description: Prepared with egg yolks, wine or vinegar or lemon-juice, and olive oil.
steps: Get two or three lettuces
Remove the faded and all the coarse green leaves, and cut the green top off
Pull the leaves off one by one, and cut them in three or four pieces, according to the size of each leaf
Well wash and drain them in a cloth
Put in a salad-bowl half a teaspoonful of salt, one or two pinches of pepper
Add the yolk of an egg or two, hard boiled, then bruise them to a pulp with the back of a wooden spoon
Add half a tablespoonful of the best wine vinegar or lemon-juice and stir it round
Pour a tablespoonful of olive oil over by degrees, and keep stirring
Add a spoonful more of vinegar, and two of oil, and beat them well up
When as smooth as cream, add the lettuce, with a tablespoonful of chopped chervil, and a teaspoonful of tarragon, one of young onions, and half-a-dozen slices or so of beet-root
Turn the salad gently till well mixed, and serve

title: Maydanosslu Yalhni
description: Prepared with mutton, onions, and lemons.
steps: Cut sufficient mutton in pieces the size of small kidneys
Boil and skim it as above
Add a few onions sliced thin and partly fried in fresh butter
Let it simmer until the meat is nearly cooked
Add two or three handfuls of picked parsley, and let it simmer for ten or fifteen minutes longer
Beat up the yolks of three or four eggs in a basin with the juice of one or two lemons
Pour it into a small saucepan, set it on a slow fire, and stir it with a wooden spoon till it begins to thicken, without permitting it to boil
Dish the stew up tastefully, pour this sauce over, and serve

title: Medkune
description: Layers of eggplant and mutton are simmered with onion, broth and lemon juice until a rich gravy remains. A small amount of cinnamon finishes the dish.

Cut two or three pounds of mutton in pieces the size of walnuts, sprinkle one or two chopped onions over with a little salt, and rub them well together with your hands

title: Menekshe Shurubi
description: Prepared with water and sugar.

ingredients.name: a pound of fresh gathered violets
ingredients.sourceText: a pound of fresh gathered violets

ingredients.name: two pints and a gill of boiling water
ingredients.sourceText: two pints and a gill of boiling water

ingredients.sourceText: about three pounds of crushed sugar

steps: Procure a pound of fresh gathered violets, cut the stalks off, and put the leaves in a basin
Pour two pints and a gill of boiling water over, immediately cover it, and let it remain for twelve or fifteen hours
Pass the liquor through a clean cloth into a stewpan, add about three pounds of crushed sugar
Stir with a wooden spoon till the sugar is dissolved, and set it on a charcoal fire
Just as it commences to boil up, instantly remove it, and let it remain covered till nearly cold
Then pass it again through a cloth, bottle and cork it up till wanted

title: Mevlevi Pilawi
description: Prepared with rice, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: a pound of rice, well washed
ingredients.sourceText: a pound of rice, well washed

ingredients.name: half a pound of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of fresh butter

steps: Put two quarts of water in a saucepan with sufficient salt, put it on the fire.
When boiling, throw into it a pound of rice, well washed, and boil until each grain is soft and separate.
Drain it through a clean cloth or in a colander, put it back in the pan, and set it on a slow fire without the cover until the moisture is dispersed.
Put a saucepan on the fire with half a pound of fresh butter.
When it boils, pour it over the rice and stir it once round with a fork, put the pan on the hob with the cover over, and let it remain for five or ten minutes.
Dish up, and serve hot.

title: Midiye-Dolmassi
description: Prepared with mussels, olive oil, and onions.

ingredients.name: three or four dozen of mussels
ingredients.sourceText: three or four dozen of mussels

ingredients.name: half a pint of olive oil
ingredients.sourceText: half a pint of olive oil

ingredients.name: two or three onions, chopped fine
ingredients.sourceText: two or three onions, chopped fine

ingredients.name: two or three ounces of pistachios, skinned
ingredients.sourceText: two or three ounces of pistachios, skinned

steps: Procure three or four dozen of mussels
Well scrape the shells in water
Wash them several times
Open them with a knife without separating one from the other
Put half a pint of olive oil in a saucepan, with two or three onions chopped fine, and set it on the fire
When hot, begin to stir with a wooden spoon until the onions are nicely browned
Add a pound of well-washed rice, two or three ounces of pistachios, skinned, and an ounce of currants, a little salt and pepper, and mixed spice
Stir till the rice begins to brown
Add a teacup of water, and keep stirring till the moisture is dispersed
Take it off
When nearly cold, stuff the mussels, and close the shells
Arrange them in a stewpan, nearly cover them with water
Place a plate over, inside downwards
Set the pan on the fire with the cover over, and let it boil until the whole of the liquid is absorbed
Dish up carefully, and serve hot or cold

Stir with a wooden spoon, and boil them until getting tender.
Cut two French penny rolls lengthwise in eight slices.
Put the yolks of two eggs in a basin, with eight tablespoonfuls of milk, and beat it up well.
Dip quickly each slice in it, and fry it a nice colour on both sides in hot fresh butter.
Lay them in a convenient pie-dish, then put the cherries over with the syrup.
If you find the syrup too thick, add a little water.
Set it on a moderate charcoal fire, and let it simmer until the syrup is absorbed, then serve.

title: Muhallebi
description: Prepared with rice, milk or water, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: about three pints of nice milk
ingredients.sourceText: about three pints of nice milk

ingredients.name: six or seven ounces of rice-flour
ingredients.sourceText: six or seven ounces of rice-flour

ingredients.name: three or four ounces of powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: three or four ounces of powdered sugar

ingredients.name: a few drops of the essence of orange-flower
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of the essence of orange-flower

steps: Pour into a stewpan about three pints of nice milk, set it on the fire
As soon as it commences to boil, put six or seven ounces of rice-flour in a basin, which mix with milk or water, to form a smooth batter
Add it gradually to the milk, with three or four ounces of powdered sugar, and a few drops of the essence of orange-flower, and keep stirring it until it forms a smooth substance, but not too thick
Pour it into a mould previously oiled with almond oil; put it on ice, or in cold water
When firm, dip the mould in warm water, turn it out on to a dish, ornament the top with pieces of clotted cream, the size of nuts, and serve

set it on the fire
When boiling, stir round with a wooden spoon until nicely browned and the moisture is dispersed

take it off, and put the meat in a basin, add two or three onions chopped very fine, one or two handfuls of picked parsley, the crumb of a French roll previously soaked in water, three or four eggs, and a little salt and pepper, and mix them well together
put a sufficient quantity of fresh butter in a convenient fryingpan, place it on a charcoal fire
When boiling, pour in the preparation
When set, and one side is nicely browned, turn it on the side, when nicely browned, dish up, and serve quite hot

title: Musannd, Khymak Baklawassi
description: Prepared with rice, milk, and eggs.

ingredients.name: white of one or two eggs
ingredients.sourceText: white of one or two eggs

steps: Prepare some pieces of paste as No. 135, and lay half of them in a baking-tin
Boil a sufficient quantity of ground rice with milk till reduced to a thick pulp
When cold, put it in a basin with the white of one or two eggs, and work it with your hands for five or ten minutes, or until you bring it to the thickness of clotted cream
Lay it all over the paste, and cover it with the remaining pieces of paste
Cut it up in diamonds, and bake it as above
Dish up tastefully, sprinkle sugar over, and serve
Cream cheese worked with a little powdered sugar may be used instead of rice

title: Muzakka
description: Prepared with mutton or lamb, onions, and broth.

ingredients.name: one or two pounds of raw mutton or lamb
ingredients.sourceText: one or two pounds of raw mutton or lamb

ingredients.name: two or three ounces of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: two or three ounces of fresh butter

ingredients.name: two or three tablespoonfuls of chopped parsley
ingredients.sourceText: two or three tablespoonfuls of chopped parsley

steps: Mince very fine one or two pounds of raw mutton or lamb
Put it in a frying-pan with two or three finely chopped onions, two or three ounces of fresh butter, and a little salt
Set it on the fire and let the meat and the onions stew a nice brown, stirring it now and then
Two minutes before taking it off, add two or three tablespoonfuls of chopped parsley and stir it well
Cut three or four egg-plants in slices lengthways and place them in salt water for ten or fifteen minutes
Place the minced meat and the egg-plants in layers into a pan
Add a pint of broth or a little more
Put the pan on a moderate charcoal fire with the cover over and let it simmer until the liquor is nearly absorbed and the egg-plants are nicely cooked
Turn it on to a dish without spoiling the shape and serve

steps: Put half a pint of the best olive-oil in a saucepan with two or three chopped onions, put it on the fire until the onions are nicely browned, stirring them now and then
Add two or three tomatos, cut in four crossways; if not in season, one or two tablespoonfuls of tomato sauce will answer
Add three or four dozen mussels with their shells open, but not separated one from another, and well scraped and washed, two pints and a half of water, and sufficient salt
When boiling, add a pound of the best rice, well washed
Put the cover over the pan, and let it simmer till the liquor is absorbed
Take it off, and place it on the hob for twenty minutes or so
Dish up, and serve hot or cold

title: Ndzli-Ash
description: Prepared with rice, rose-water, and powdered sugar.
steps: Pound, rather coarse, half a pound of rice in a mortar
Put three pints of water in a stewpan with a wine-glass of rose-water
Set it on the fire
When boiling, add the rice
Let it simmer till nearly thick, stirring it now and then
Sweeten it with powdered sugar according to taste
Let it simmer for a few minutes longer
Pour it in a dish
When cold, sprinkle some powdered almonds or walnuts over
Serve

description: Prepared with beef or mutton, onions, and eggs.
steps: Mince a sufficient quantity of raw beef or mutton together with two or three onions
Pound it well in a mortar with an equal quantity of Pilaw
Break over it three or four eggs
Sprinkle sufficient salt and pepper, with a handful of parsley chopped fine
Knead well all together, and let it remain covered for half an hour
Divide it in pieces the size of an egg
Fry them in boiling fresh butter
When all are nicely browned, dish up tastefully, and serve hot

title: Nevi Digher
description: Prepared with meat, onions, and grated cheese.
steps: Put sufficient flour upon a pastry slab, make a hole in the centre, in which put a little salt, two or three ounces of fresh butter melted
Mix all together, then add sufficient water, and make it a softish paste
While working it, dip your hands in butter now and then, and knead it till a nice paste is formed
Throw some flour lightly over and under, roll it out with a rolling-pin to the thickness of half-a-crown
Put a tablespoonful of fried minced meat on it, mixed with finely-chopped onions stewed brown in fresh butter, or grated cheese, about an inch and a half distance from each other
Wet lightly round them with a paste-brush, and place a similar piece of paste over all
Press round the part where the minced meat or cheese is, to make the paste stick
Cut them out like half an egg, and fry them in hot butter
When nicely browned, take them out, and let them drain, dish up

Put them before the fire, and turn them gently
As soon as the gravy begins to drop, sprinkle a little flour over

title: Nevi Digher
description: Prepared with meat, onions, and flour.

ingredients.name: two or three ounces of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: two or three ounces of fresh butter

steps: Put sufficient flour upon a pastry slab, make a hole in the centre, in which put a little salt, two or three ounces of fresh butter melted, mix all together, then add sufficient water, and make it a softish paste.
While working it, dip your hands in butter now and then, and knead it till a nice paste is formed.
Throw some flour lightly over and under, roll it out with a rolling-pin to the thickness of half-a-crown.
Put a tablespoonful of fried minced meat on it, mixed with finely-chopped onions stewed brown in fresh butter, or grated cheese, about an inch and a half distance from each other.
Wet lightly round them with a paste-brush, and place a similar piece of paste over all.
Press round the part where the minced meat or cheese is, to make the paste stick.
Cut them out like half an egg, and fry them in hot butter.
When nicely browned, take them out, and let them drain, dish up.

description: Prepared with quinces, powdered sugar, and water.

Put them in a stewpan with 4 quarts of water
Set the pan on the fire and let it boil until the fruit becomes like a jelly

Add 3 pounds of powdered sugar

Take it off and strain it again
Try a little on a plate before potting to see if it sets
When nearly cold, fill your preserve jars and cover them when cold

title: Nevi Digler
description: Prepared with beef, vinegar, and orange-peel.
steps: Get in one piece five or six pounds of the leg or rump of beef
Cover it with vinegar, and let it remain four and twenty hours
Wash it, and make deep holes all over
Fill the holes with pepper-corns, orange-peel, and cloves of garlic peeled
Place it in a stewpan with three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter
Set it on a moderate charcoal fire for three or four hours, turning it now and then
When nicely browned, add the juice of two or three pounds of tomatoes with two or three pints of water, and sufficient salt and pepper
Let it simmer till the meat is nicely cooked
Take it out, and keep it hot
Put in the stewpan about two pounds and a half of the best macaroni
If the liquor is not enough, add some of the broth, and boil till the macaroni is tender
Let it be rather firm to the touch
Dish it up, sprinkle some finely-grated cheese over, then place the beef in the centre of the macaroni, and serve

ingredients.name: juice of two or three lemons

steps: Get four or five pounds of loin of mutton, remove the bones, and cut the meat in pieces the size of walnuts
Add six or seven onions sliced fine
Sprinkle sufficient salt and pepper over, mix them all together, and rub them well with your hands
Peel four or five vegetable marrows, and cut them in slices; take out the insides, if seeded

Lay the bones of the mutton on the bottom of a convenient stewpan; then some slices of vegetable marrow over, then some pieces of mutton, then vegetable marrow, and so forth, till you have laid the whole
Cover them with water, add the juice of two or three lemons and a little salt
Set it on the fire, and let it simmer gently until the meat and the vegetable marrows are tender
Add three or four teaspoonfuls of powdered sugar, four or five cloves of garlic, skinned and well pounded, and two or three tablespoonfuls of chopped mint
Let it simmer for five or six minutes longer, then dish it up, and serve

Add one tablespoonful at a time, three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter, previously melted, and a quarter of a pound of skinned almonds

title: Nevi Higher
description: Prepared with lamb, onions, and juice.

ingredients.name: six or seven dozens of young okras

title: Chickpea soup with cinnamon and toast
description: Cooked chickpeas are pureed with broth into a smooth, earthy soup. A small dusting of cinnamon and crisp toasted bread cubes add warmth and texture without a heavy cream finish.

steps: Blend {{chickpeas}} with {{broth}} until very smooth. For a finer texture, press through a sieve and scrape the underside into a saucepan.

title: Nuriye
description: Prepared with lemons, olive oil or butter, and syrup.
steps: Put in a basin or on a slab one pound of flour
Make a hole in the centre, in which put a small teaspoonful of salt, the white of five or six eggs, and the juice of two or three lemons strained
Mix all together
Dip your hands in olive oil or butter
Work it until it forms a softish flexible paste
Divide it in pieces the size of walnuts
Roll them out to the thickness of a sixpence with a rolling-pin
Fold each piece even
Fry them a nice brown in scalded fresh butter and put them in a colander
When free from fat, throw them in boiling syrup, which you have previously made of loaf sugar and water as in No. 149
Take them out and lay half of them in a baking-tin, one over the other
Lay all over some clotted cream, about a quarter of an inch thick
Cover it with the other half of the paste
Add half a pint of milk, or little more
Put it on a charcoal fire and let it boil until quite soft
Sprinkle some rose-water over, with a little powdered cinnamon, and serve

title: Pacha-Bureghi
description: Prepared with calf's head, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: half a calf's head or four of the feet
ingredients.sourceText: half a calf's head or four of the feet

steps: Get half a calf's head, or four of the feet, wash, and put them in a stewpan with sufficient water and salt
Set it on the fire, and let it boil until tender
Remove the meat from the bones, and cut it in small dice
Prepare ten or twelve pieces of paste as No. 78, but instead of scalding them in water, scald them in boiling fresh butter

When all done, take out and place them in a colander, and when free from fat, lay half of them in a rather deep and circular baking-tin one over the other, sprinkling between each piece some of the liquor in which the calf's head is boiled
Lay the pieces of calf's head all over, cover them with the remaining pieces of paste the same way as before, and bake it a nice colour
Dish up, and serve

description: Prepared with wine or vinegar or juice or lemons, toast, and juice or lemon.

ingredients.name: half a teacup of wine vinegar or the juice of three or four lemons

steps: Clean the sheep's trotters and break the long bones
Put them in a stewpan nearly full of water
Place it on the fire or in a very hot oven with the cover over it until the meat comes off the bones
Take out the large bones and cut the meat in small pieces
Pound three or four cloves of garlic in a mortar with a little salt
Add half a teacup of wine vinegar or the juice of three or four lemons and stir it well with a wooden spoon
Pour it over the trotters with a little salt and stir it once
Set it on the fire and let it boil again for two or three minutes
Lay thin slices of toast on the bottom of a dish, over which place the pieces of trotters with some of the liquor
Put it on a very slow charcoal fire until the liquor is nearly absorbed
Beat up the yolks of two or three eggs with the juice of a lemon or two and a little of the liquor in which the trotters are cooked
Place them on a moderate fire and begin stirring with a wooden spoon (taking it from the fire now and then when getting too hot) until it thickens
Pour it over the trotters, sprinkle a little pepper and cinnamon over, and serve very hot

title: Pdhati-l-hdlkum
description: A rose-flavored wheat-starch confection cooked until thick, cooled in a shallow pan and cut into pieces. A sugar-and-starch coating keeps the pieces from sticking; the historic musk flavoring needs a modern replacement.

ingredients.name: two pounds and three-quarters of loaf-sugar
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds and three-quarters of loaf-sugar

ingredients.name: eight ounces and a half of fine wheat starch
ingredients.sourceText: eight ounces and a half of fine wheat starch

ingredients.name: a little less than a quarter of a pint of rose-water
ingredients.sourceText: a little less than a quarter of a pint of rose-water

ingredients.name: sifted sugar mixed with fine wheat starch
ingredients.sourceText: sifted sugar mixed with fine wheat starch

steps: Put in a very clean stewpan two pounds and three-quarters of loaf-sugar, with four quarts of water
Stir with a wooden spoon until the sugar is dissolved
Set it on a moderate charcoal fire
Immediately add eight ounces and a half of fine wheat starch by degrees, stirring it at the same time so as to prevent it from getting lumpy
Continue stirring it from the bottom of the pan until it forms a smooth substance
Take a little out and let drop a few drops on powdered sugar
If it moistens or absorbs the sugar it is not done, and if it does not it is done
Mix a little musk, the size of a small pea, in a little less than a quarter of a pint of rose-water and add this to it
Stir it for half a minute or a minute longer
Take it off and pour it into a convenient dish or a plated pan about an inch deep, which you have previously oiled with almond-oil
When cold, cut it in pieces an inch broad and two long
Dip them in sifted sugar mixed with half the quantity of fine wheat starch
See that they are well covered, to prevent them from sticking to each other
Serve as a dessert

title: Pdlude
description: A molded wheat-starch dessert flavored with rose or orange-flower essence. The sweet mixture is chilled until firm and may be decorated with pistachios or almonds.

ingredients.name: about five ounces of wheat starch
ingredients.sourceText: about five ounces of wheat starch

steps: Dissolve {{source-0}} in a stewpan, with two quarts of water
Add about five ounces of wheat starch and stir it well
When as smooth as milk, put it on a moderate charcoal fire
Continually stir it for about three hours, or until it forms a smooth substance, but not too thick
Add a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower
Stir it for a few minutes longer
Pour it into a mould previously oiled with almond-oil
Put it on ice, or in a cool place, till firm
When ready, dip the mould in warm water and turn it out
Serve (you can ornament the top with some skinned pistachios or almonds)

title: Pirmj-Unu Helivassi
description: Prepared with rice, almonds, and syrup.

ingredients.name: a pound of the best fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: a pound of the best fresh butter

ingredients.name: a pound and a half of rice-flour
ingredients.sourceText: a pound and a half of rice-flour

ingredients.name: a quarter of a pound of skinned almonds

ingredients.name: a pint and a half of boiling syrup
ingredients.sourceText: a pint and a half of boiling syrup

ingredients.name: a pint and a half of boiling milk

steps: Put in a stewpan a pound of the best fresh butter, and scald it
Then remove it from the fire: when a little cold, add by degrees a pound and a half of rice-flour
Set it again on the fire, and keep stirring for twenty-five minutes, or until the butter appears on the surface of the flour, and the flour swells up like grains of gunpowder
Then add a quarter of a pound of skinned almonds, and stir it for a few minutes longer
Then immediately add a pint and a half of boiling syrup, previously prepared of white sugar and water, as in No. 159, and the same quantity of boiling milk
Instantly put the cover over, and let it remain for about five minutes
Then stir it well with a wooden fork, dish it up in spoonfuls, and let it bear the impression of the spoon
Sprinkle a little powdered sugar over, and serve

title: Portakal Elmassiyyessi
description: Prepared with oranges, powdered sugar, and isinglass.

ingredients.name: five or six ounces of powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: five or six ounces of powdered sugar

ingredients.name: a few drops of prepared cochineal
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of prepared cochineal

steps: Get six nice oranges, take off the rind of one of them, and remove the pith, place them in a basin, and squeeze the juice of the oranges in it
Put five or six ounces of powdered sugar in a saucepan with half a pint of water, and boil it until it becomes a syrup
Take it off, and add the juice and the rind of the oranges; put the saucepan again on the fire with the cover over
As soon as it begins to boil, skim it well, and add gradually a small teacup of water; let it boil one or two minutes longer
Add an ounce of isinglass, dissolved as directed; stir well, and pass it through a jelly-bag till clear
Add a few drops of prepared cochineal, and pour it in a mould; place it on ice until firm
Turn it out as before, and serve

title: Reward
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, sago, and butter.

ingredients.name: one pound and a quarter of the best fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: one pound and a quarter of the best fresh butter

ingredients.name: one pound and a quarter of powdered sugar

ingredients.name: two pounds and two ounces of sago

ingredients.name: three quarters of a pound of loaf sugar
ingredients.sourceText: three quarters of a pound of loaf sugar

steps: Put in a basin a pound and a quarter of the best fresh butter, and work it well with clean hands until it is like a cream
Break in twelve eggs, and beat up well together
Mix in by degrees one pound and a quarter of powdered sugar
While beating up, add gradually two pounds and two ounces of sago, and keep beating it up for a few minutes longer
Butter a rather deep baking-tin, in which pour the preparation
Bake it a nice colour in a hot oven
Dissolve three quarters of a pound of loaf sugar in seven pints of water, and keep it lukewarm
When the pudding is nicely browned, pour gradually some of the sherbet or sugar and water all over with a ladle
Put it again in the oven until the sherbet is absorbed, and continue in this manner until you have used the whole of the sherbet
Cut it up in diamonds, dish up tastefully, shake some powdered sugar over, and serve

title: Sach-Bureghi
description: Prepared with beef or mutton, onions, and flour.

ingredients.name: one or two pounds of flour
ingredients.sourceText: one or two pounds of flour

steps: Put in a basin one or two pounds of flour, and a little salt, mix it with sufficient water into a softish paste with your hands
Dry it off a little with flour till you have well cleared the paste from the basin, and let it remain for two or three minutes
Cut it into ten or twelve pieces, and roll them round with a rolling-pin the size of a dinner-plate, and as thin as a wafer

Lay some finely-minced raw beef or mutton, mixed with a small quantity of onions chopped very fine, a little salt, pepper, and cinnamon over one half of each piece, half a quarter of an inch thick, and double the other half over
Press the two edges with your fingers to make the paste stick
Put a trevet on a charcoal fire, over which place a slightly-domed sheet-iron, the under side of which is previously cemented with ashes, to prevent it from getting fiercely hot
When moderately hot, dip a paste-brush in fresh butter, previously melted, and rub it all over
Place the pieces of paste over, and bake them a nice brown on both sides, now and then buttering them on both sides with the paste-brush
When done, take them off with a slice, dish them up one over the other, and serve hot

title: Serai Lhmmassi
description: Prepared with biscuit, cochineal, and orange.

ingredients.name: half a pound of plain white biscuit
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of plain white biscuit

ingredients.name: a pound and a quarter of loaf sugar
ingredients.sourceText: a pound and a quarter of loaf sugar

steps: Pound in a mortar half a pound of plain white biscuit and sift it through a fine sieve
Beat up the whites of twenty eggs in a basin
Add by degrees the powdered biscuit and beat it up together until it forms a smooth consistency
Take it up a dessertspoonful at a time and pour it into boiling fresh butter one after the other
Fry them a nice delicate brown; they should be round and swell up to the size of a peach
When done, drain and place them in a stewpan half full of boiling water
Let them boil for ten minutes or so
Take it off and strain the water from them
Dissolve a pound and a quarter of loaf sugar in as much water as will cover them
Add a few drops of prepared cochineal with a few drops of the essence of orange-flower or rose and stir it well
Pour it over them and set the pan on a charcoal fire with the cover over
Let it boil until the syrup is nearly absorbed
Dish up and serve hot or cold

Take out with a wooden spoon what pulp there is on the top, and put it in a basin, add some more water, and continue so until you have extracted all the goodness from the grains
Strain the remaining grains through a sieve, and put all the pulp you have collected into a saucepan
Add two or three ounces of washed currants, and a quarter or half a pound of loaf sugar, previously made into syrup
Put it on a charcoal fire and begin stirring it
When boiling, add a little musk mixed with two or three tablespoonfuls of rose-water, and stir it one or two minutes longer
Take it off and pour it into a dish, arrange on the top tastefully some skinned almonds and pistachios, and serve when cold

title: Shalghdm Dolmessi
description: Prepared with turnips, mutton, and onions.

ingredients.name: two or three tablespoonfuls of wine vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: two or three tablespoonfuls of wine vinegar

ingredients.name: one tablespoonful of honey or powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: one tablespoonful of honey or powdered sugar

steps: Peel half a dozen middle-sized turnips, and hollow them out
Mince sufficient raw mutton, add two finely chopped onions, a little chopped parsley, a handful of well-cleaned rice, and a little salt and pepper
Mix well all together with the hands
Stuff the turnips with it, and place the lids over
Place them in a stewpan, and nearly cover them with broth
Add a little salt
Put the pan on the fire with the cover over, and let it simmer until the turnips are nearly soft
Add two or three tablespoonfuls of wine vinegar, and one of honey or powdered sugar
When sufficient gravy is left, and the turnips are quite done, dish up tastefully, and serve

steps: Cut in four crossways, without separating from the stalk, six or eight egg-plants, not seeded
Cut out part of the inside of each one, and throw it away, and put the egg-plants in brine
Put in a fryingpan two or three ounces of fresh butter, one or two pounds of minced raw mutton, three or four finely chopped onions, and fry them a nice brown
Add two or three tablespoonfuls of parsley, chopped fine, the same of mint, sufficient salt and pepper, and mix them well together
Stuff the egg-plants with this, and tie them up separately with the stalks of parsley
Cover the bottom of a stewpan with some peeled parsley roots, in which lay the stuffed egg-plants, and cover them with mutton broth, or with the broth (No. 1)
Set the pan on the fire with the cover over
When boiling, let it simmer until a nice thick gravy is formed at the bottom
Dish them up tastefully one over the other, and serve, or dress them with some curd, flavoured with a little garlic, if approved of, then serve

ingredients.name: loin or leg of mutton

ingredients.name: half a dozen tomatos or four or five tablespoonfuls of preserved tomato sauce

steps: Cut {{source-0}} in pieces the size of an egg
Chop four middle-sized onions, and sprinkle them over the meat with sufficient salt, pepper, and cinnamon

Pass the pieces of meat one by one on the skewers, place them in front of the fire, and gradually turn them
As soon as the meat begins to brown, baste it now and then with the tomato juice
When nicely cooked, dish it up, and serve hot

title: Sighir-eti Ydhni
description: Prepared with steak, garlic, and potatoes.
steps: Cut five or six pounds of rump-steak into rather long slices, half or three-quarters of an inch thick
Tie them together one over the other with a piece of string, as if one piece of meat
With the point of a knife, make about fifteen holes here and there, and stick in each a clove of garlic peeled
Place it in a stewpan with about three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter, set it on a moderate charcoal fire with the cover over for about three hours, turning the meat every half hour
Add two or three pounds of sliced potatoes partly fried in butter, and the juice of two or three pounds of ripe tomatoes with a little water, and sufficient salt and pepper
Put the cover over the pan and let it simmer until the meat and the potatoes are well done
Cut the string off the meat, dish up tastefully, and serve

description: Prepared with meat or cheese, flour, and salt.
steps: Put on the dresser, or in a basin, sufficient quantity of flour, with a little salt
Mix it up with as many eggs as it will take, and form it a softish flexible paste
Cut it in twelve or fourteen pieces, and roll them out the size of the baking-tin intended for laying them in
Fill a saucepan or iron pot with water, put in sufficient salt, and set it on the fire
When boiling, scald the pieces of paste one by one, except two
When done, drain them, then dry them with a piece of clean cloth, and spread out the wrinkled parts carefully
Put some fresh butter in a saucepan, and set it on the fire
When the butter is at proper heat, take it off, and when rather cold, butter the baking-tin with it
In the baking-tin lay one of the two unscalded pieces of paste, sprinkle a tablespoonful of the butter over
Lay half of the scalded pieces, sprinkling between each one a spoonful of butter
Lay minced meat or cheese all over, half an inch thick
Cover it with the remaining pieces of paste that are scalded, sprinkling some butter between each one as before
Lay the other unscalded piece over, well butter the top, and place it in a hot oven
When nicely browned, cut it in any shape you choose, dish up, and serve hot

title: Sungheriye
description: Prepared with rice, eggs, and milk.

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pound of ground rice
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pound of ground rice

ingredients.name: a few drops of the essence of rose, or any other essence
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of the essence of rose, or any other essence

ingredients.name: five or six pints of milk
ingredients.sourceText: five or six pints of milk

steps: Put in a basin the white of forty eggs, and beat them up until they are formed into a firm froth
Add by degrees three-quarters of a pound of ground rice, with a few drops of the essence of rose, or any other essence you fancy
Beat it up again for some time
Put into a saucepan five or six pints of milk, and set it on a charcoal fire
When boiling, throw in a tablespoonful of the mixture at a time, which will be done in a few minutes
Take it out with a hand-strainer, and throw it into boiling syrup, which you have previously prepared, of sugar and water
Take it out again with the hand-strainer after a few seconds, and place it in a dish
Continue in this manner until the whole is done, and serve

title: Sussiiz Pilaw
description: Prepared with mutton or lamb, rice, and salt.

ingredients.name: mutton or lamb
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds of mutton or lamb

ingredients.name: two pounds and a half of rice
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds and a half of rice

ingredients.name: half a pound of hot fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of hot fresh butter

ingredients.name: half a dozen pieces of gum-mastic

ingredients.name: two or three pieces of cinnamon

steps: Cut {{source-0}} into pieces the size of walnuts, wash them, sprinkle them with sufficient salt and pepper, and lay them on the bottom of a stewpan with a tight-fitting cover.
Well wash two pounds and a half of rice, and place it over the meat.

Pour half a pound of hot fresh butter over, add half a dozen pieces of gum-mastic, two or three pieces of cinnamon, put the cover over the pan contrariwise, wrap a wet cloth round it, and fill the cover with water.
Set the pan on a slow charcoal fire, and let it simmer for about four hours.
Take off the cover, and turn the contents carefully on to a hot dish, and serve.

title: Sussuz Kyufte
description: Prepared with mutton, onion, and salt.

ingredients.name: a quarter of a pound of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: a quarter of a pound of fresh butter

steps: Mince very fine as much as is required of the best part of raw mutton
Sprinkle a little salt, pepper, and cinnamon over
Knead well with a little onion juice, and make it into balls the size of walnuts
Put in a bowl or basin a teacup of water, and a quarter of a pound of fresh butter
Arrange the balls of meat in the bowl, and place it into an iron pot
Put the cover over and paste it round, or wrap a wet cloth round it, so as to prevent the steam from escaping
Set it on a moderate fire, and let it simmer for about two hours
Dish it up tastefully, and serve hot

title: Sutlu-Ash
description: Prepared with rice, powdered sugar, and milk.

ingredients.name: the best rice
ingredients.sourceText: six ounces of the best rice

ingredients.name: two pints and three-quarters of nice milk
ingredients.sourceText: two pints and three-quarters of nice milk

steps: Wash and scald {{source-0}}
Drain it
Pour into a stewpan two pints and three-quarters of nice milk
Set it on the fire
As soon as it commences to boil, add the rice
Let it simmer until quite soft
Take it off and pour it into a pie-dish
Put it on a very slow charcoal fire, covered with ashes, or on the hob
Let it remain for about fifteen minutes, during which time the top of the rice will be covered with cream
When cold, sprinkle sufficient powdered sugar over
Serve (You may sweeten the rice while boiling, and add one or two tablespoonfuls of rose-water)

title: Tarhhctna Chbrbassi
description: Prepared with rolls, curd, and broth.

ingredients.name: two pounds and a half of crumbs of French rolls
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds and a half of crumbs of French rolls

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pound of curd
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pound of curd

steps: Put two pounds and a half of crumbs of French rolls in a stone mortar, with three-quarters of a pound of curd
Pound them well together, and let it remain for one night
Put it in a stewpan, and moisten it by degrees with as much broth as is required by bruising and beating it up smooth with a wooden spoon
Set it on a moderate fire, and let it simmer for about an hour
Take it off, and pour it into a tureen, and serve it with bread cut into small dice and fried in fresh butter
The addition of a small quantity of cream or milk will render it still more pleasant

description: Prepared with scallops, onions, and rice.

ingredients.name: two or three dozen of small scallops
ingredients.sourceText: two or three dozen of small scallops

ingredients.name: six or seven ounces of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: six or seven ounces of fresh butter

ingredients.name: a pound of the best rice, well washed

ingredients.name: half a teacup of the best olive-oil

steps: Procure two or three dozen of small scallops, scrape and well wash them, and open the shells without separating one from the other
Put six or seven ounces of fresh butter in a pan, with two or three finely-chopped onions
Set it on the fire, and fry them partly brown
Add a pound of the best rice, well washed, a little salt and pepper, and stir it with a wooden spoon for ten minutes or so
Stuff the scallops with the rice, and place them carefully in a convenient saucepan, with half a teacup of the best olive-oil
Cover them with water, put a plate over upside downwards, put the lid on, and let it simmer on a moderate fire until there is no liquid remaining
Arrange them in a dish, and serve, hot or cold

title: Tawshan Kebabi
description: Prepared with hare, garlic, and wine.
steps: Procure a nice hare, clean it well, cut it into pieces, each about the size of a kidney
Put them in cold water, and let them remain for two or three hours
Take them out, and dry them in a cloth, season with sufficient salt and pepper, and let them remain for twenty minutes or so
Pass them on the skewers one by one, put them before a moderate fire
While they are turning, peel five or six cloves of garlic, and well pound them in a mortar with a little salt
Add a small teacup of wine vinegar, stir it well, pour it in a small saucepan, add a quarter of a pound of fresh butter
Place the saucepan on a moderate charcoal fire, and stir well with a wooden spoon until the butter is melted
Take off, and keep it hot

title: Tawuh Ydhni
description: Prepared with fowl, mutton, and onions.
steps: Cut a well-cleaned fowl in two lengthways
Place it in a stewpan with two or three pounds of the middle of a neck of mutton
Cover them with water, put in a little salt
Set it on the fire, and let it boil till the fowl is half cooked, and skim it well
Take the fowl out and fry it a nice colour in fresh butter

Place it in a stewpan with six or eight sliced onions fried in butter, a pint and a quarter of chick-peas, previously boiled a little soft and skinned, two or three tablespoonfuls of wine vinegar, and the liquor in which the fowl is boiled
Add sufficient salt and pepper

title: Tawuk Kyul-Basstissi
description: Prepared with fowls, broth, and salt.
steps: Split one or two nice fowls lengthways, and remove the whole of the bones with a sharp knife
Cut the flesh in four or five pieces as you fancy, and beat the thicker parts even with a rolling pin
Sprinkle them with sufficient salt and pepper, and a little cinnamon, and let them remain for one or two hours
Place them on a gridiron, set it on a moderate charcoal fire, and constantly turn them with a pair of tongs
When nicely browned, lay them in a stewpan, and cover them with broth
Put the pan on a moderate charcoal fire, and let simmer until tender
Dish up, and serve hot

description: Prepared with chickens, chicken broth, and rice.

ingredients.name: a pound and a half of rice, well washed
ingredients.sourceText: a pound and a half of rice, well washed

ingredients.name: a quarter of a pound of fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: a quarter of a pound of fresh butter

ingredients.name: two or three pieces of cinnamon

steps: Place one or two nice chickens in a saucepan, and nearly fill it with water, add a little salt, and set it on the fire.
When boiling, skim and simmer until the chickens are tender.
Take them out, place them in a dish, and keep them hot.

Measure three pints of the broth of the chickens, and pour it in a pan, to which add a pound and a half of rice, well washed, a quarter of a pound of fresh butter, half a dozen pieces of gum-mastic, two or three pieces of cinnamon, and half a teaspoonful of salt.
Put the pan on the fire with the cover over, and let it boil gently until the liquor is absorbed.
Take it off, stir it once round with a fork, and keep it on the hob with the cover over for fifteen or twenty minutes.
Take out the pieces of cinnamon.
Dish up the rice, in the centre of which place the chickens, cut in pieces, and serve very hot.

title: Tdss Kebdbi
description: Prepared with mutton, onions, and broth.
steps: Cut sufficient quantity of a leg or loin of mutton in pieces the size of small walnuts
Wash them with cold water, and dry them in a cloth
Sprinkle two or three finely-chopped onions over, with sufficient salt, pepper, and mixed spice
Rub them well in the meat, and let it remain covered for about two hours

Put the pieces of meat in a convenient basin, and place it upside downwards in the centre of a clean baking-tin an inch and a half deep, and the bottom of which must be strong enough to bear the heat of the fire
Place a trevet on a charcoal fire, and over which set the baking-tin for about an hour and a half
When the gravy has run out and is absorbed, pour in the baking-tin a pint and a half of broth No. 1 or No. 2, and add three-quarters of a pound of the best rice, well washed
Spread it even around the basin
When the broth is absorbed, and the rice is hard, sprinkle some more broth over
Each grain should be soft, and well separated
When done, take the baking-tin off the fire, and just at the time it is wanted, remove the basin from the centre of it, and serve as it is, with a napkin pinned round the baking-tin

Add a little mixed spice, salt, and pepper, the juice of one or two lemons, the yolks of two or three eggs, and a little water, and beat them up well together with a wooden spoon

Put it on the fire, and just scald it
Add half a pint of water, half a teaspoonful of salt

Dish up tastefully, and serve hot

Put it on the fire until the lights are nearly cooked
Add three or four pints of broth, and let it simmer till the pieces of lights are quite done
Beat up the yolks of two or three eggs in a small saucepan, with the juice of one or two lemons, or with a little wine vinegar, and stir it on a slow fire with a wooden spoon till a little thick
Take it off and pour it gradually into the soup, stirring it quickly at the same time, to prevent the eggs from curdling
Pour the soup into a tureen, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

steps: Prepare a pound and a quarter of fresh butter, break six eggs over, and beat up well together
Add gradually two pounds and a half of the best honey or powdered sugar, previously made into a syrup, and beat them up well
Add by degrees about two pounds and a half of nice sago, bringing it to the consistency of a thick batter
Pour it in a rather deep baking-tin, previously buttered
Bake it a nice brown in a hot oven
Dissolve five or six ounces of loaf-sugar in about three pints of water, with half a teacup of rose-water, and keep it lukewarm
When the pudding is nicely done, pour it all over, and put it again in the oven
When the whole of the liquid is absorbed, take it out, cut it up in any shape you fancy, dish up, and serve with powdered sugar over
