title: Thwuh Ghyuhssu
description: Prepared with chickens, rice flour, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: five pints and a half of nice milk
ingredients.sourceText: five pints and a half of nice milk

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pound of rice flour
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pound of rice flour

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pound of powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pound of powdered sugar

ingredients.name: one or two tablespoonfuls of rose-water
ingredients.sourceText: one or two tablespoonfuls of rose-water

steps: Boil two or three chickens.
When done, cut off the breasts, remove the bones and the skins from them, and pound the meat in a stone mortar, or pull it in bits like fine threads.
Pour in a stewpan five pints and a half of nice milk, put it on the fire.
While boiling, put in a basin three-quarters of a pound of rice flour, which mix with some of the boiling milk and some water, to form a batter.
Add this to the milk and boil it until it becomes a smooth substance, but not too thick.
Add the pounded breasts of chickens with three-quarters of a pound of powdered sugar, and one or two tablespoonfuls of rose-water.
Keep stirring, and at the same time beating it up on a slow fire until it forms a rather thick glutinous substance.

title: Turk Bureghi
description: Prepared with flour, salt, and eggs.
steps: Put on the dresser a pound of flour, make a hole in the centre, in which put a teaspoonful of salt
Break in two eggs, mix all together
Add sufficient water, and form it a softish flexible paste
Divide it in two, and roll them out to the size of the baking-tin you intend to use
Sprinkle some melted fresh butter over, and fold over the edges of the paste so as to hide the butter
Throw a little flour both under and over, and roll them out again as before
Repeat the same five or six times more
Butter the baking-tin, in which lay one of the two pieces of paste
Lay any preparation you choose all over it, half an inch thick, and cover it with the other paste
Make about fifteen deep holes in the paste here and there with the point of a knife
Bake it a nice brown on both sides
When done, cut it in diamonds, dish up tastefully, and serve hot

title: Uskkumru Tāwassi
description: Prepared with mackerel, onions, and juice.

ingredients.name: juice of two or three lemons
ingredients.sourceText: juice of two or three lemons

ingredients.name: yolks of three or four eggs
ingredients.sourceText: yolks of three or four eggs

steps: Take out the insides and the gills of half a dozen middle-sized mackerel, wash well, and sprinkle them with a little salt, and let them remain twenty minutes or so.

Peel two or three onions, and well pound them in a mortar, to which add sufficient salt and pepper, mixed spice, the juice of two or three lemons, and the yolks of three or four eggs, and well beat them up.
Pour it into a pie-dish, roll the mackerel in it, and let them remain for about two hours.
Fry them a nice brown in hot olive oil, turning them over.
When done, take them out with a slice and let them drain well, dish them up tastefully, squeeze a lemon over, if approved of, and serve hot.

description: Prepared with mackerel, onions, and olive oil.

ingredients.name: half a teacup of wine vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: half a teacup of wine vinegar

ingredients.name: two or three teacups of water

ingredients.name: a tablespoonful of preserved tomato sauce

steps: Take out the inside of half a dozen mackerel and wash them
Boil them in water for one or two minutes
When cold, remove the bones
Cut three or four onions in slices and fry them partly brown in olive oil
Lay the half on the bottom of a stewpan with a handful of picked parsley mixed with a little fennel
Pour in what oil is left in the frying-pan
Place the pieces of mackerel over
Put the other half of the onions with the same quantity of parsley and fennel on the top
Add half a teacup of wine vinegar and two or three teacups of the water in which the fish is boiled
Add sufficient salt and pepper
Put the pan on a moderate charcoal fire with the lid on and let it simmer gently for about fifteen or twenty minutes until the fish is nicely done
Dish it up, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

description: Prepared with grapes and mustard.

ingredients.sourceText: ten or twelve pounds of black or white grapes

steps: Pick out the best bunches of grapes
Squeeze the juice from the bruised and small ones
Pass it through a sieve into a stewpan free from smell
Set it to boil for a few minutes
Wash the bunches you have selected
Lay two or three of them on the bottom of a stone jar
Sprinkle some mustard-seeds over, then grapes, again mustard-seeds over, then grapes, continuing so till the whole of the grapes are laid
Pour the boiled grape-juice over
Cover the jar air-tight and let it remain for thirty or forty days before using

title: Yaghsiz Balik Yahnissi
description: Prepared with onions, garlic, and lemon.

ingredients.name: three or four heads of garlic
ingredients.sourceText: three or four heads of garlic

ingredients.name: two or three handfuls of parsley
ingredients.sourceText: two or three handfuls of parsley

steps: Get six or seven red mullets, take out the insides, well clean them, and sprinkle some salt over
Put three pints of water in a saucepan with three or four onions cut in four crossways and three or four heads of garlic with only the outer skins peeled
Put it on the fire and let boil until the water is reduced to about one pint
Take the onions and the garlic out, throw the onions away, but squeeze the garlic and add the pulp to the liquor
Peel two or three onions and chop them very fine with two or three handfuls of parsley
Sprinkle a little salt and pepper over and well rub them
Stuff the fish with it and lay it carefully in a stewpan
Pour the liquor over, set it on a charcoal fire and let it simmer till the fish is nicely cooked
Dish it up, squeeze half a lemon over, and serve hot

title: Yalcinji-Bahk-Dholmassi
description: Prepared with olive oil or butter, onions, and rice.

ingredients.name: half a dozen rather thin and long egg-plants
ingredients.sourceText: half a dozen rather thin and long egg-plants

ingredients.name: half a pound of well-washed rice
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of well-washed rice

ingredients.name: half a teacup of hot water
ingredients.sourceText: half a teacup of hot water

steps: Peel egg-plants very thin in spots here and there (imitating the fish scales)
Cut off the tops, as large as a florin, and take out the whole of the inside, leaving only sufficient to bear stuffing
Throw them in salt water for ten or fifteen minutes
Put four or five ounces of nice olive oil or fresh butter in a saucepan, and set it on the fire
When hot, add three or four onions chopped fine, and begin stirring it with a wooden spoon
When on the point of browning, add half a pound of well-washed rice, and keep stirring
As soon as the rice begins to brown, pour in half a teacup of hot water, and continue stirring
When the water is absorbed, add another half a teacup of water, and keep stirring
When the rice is partly soft, add the half of a white plain biscuit, well powdered, {{source-7}}, one of currants, sufficient salt, pepper, and a little mixed spice; stir well; then take it off
When partly cold, stuff the egg-plants with it, and cover them with the tops contrariwise
Cover the bottom of a saucepan with some rib-bones of mutton, and place the egg-plants over
Cover them with water, set the pan on the fire with the lid over, and let it simmer till the egg-plants are partly soft
Take them out and fry them a nice colour in hot olive oil or fresh butter
Dish them up tastefully, and serve

title: Yalcinji-Ddlmci
description: Prepared with olive oil, onions, and rice.

ingredients.name: seven or eight dozens of young vine leaves
ingredients.sourceText: seven or eight dozens of young vine leaves

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pint of olive oil
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pint of olive oil

ingredients.name: two pounds and a half of finely chopped onions
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds and a half of finely chopped onions

ingredients.name: two pounds and a half of the best rice
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds and a half of the best rice

ingredients.name: one or two teaspoonfuls of powdered mint
ingredients.sourceText: one or two teaspoonfuls of powdered mint

steps: Procure seven or eight dozens of young vine leaves, and scald them
Let them drain in a colander
Pour in a saucepan three-quarters of a pint of olive oil and place it on the fire
When hot, put in two pounds and a half of finely chopped onions, and stir until they begin to brown
Add two pounds and a half of the best rice, well cleaned, and keep stirring
When the rice is on the point of browning, add two teacupfuls of water, and continue stirring gently till the water is absorbed
Take it off, add one or two teaspoonfuls of powdered mint, a little salt, pepper, and cinnamon, and well stir it
Spread the vine leaves out, and put half a tablespoonful of the prepared rice in each one
Fold it about the length of your thumb, but a little thicker, and squeeze it gently in your hand, so that it may not open while cooking
Cover the bottom of a saucepan with rib-bones of mutton, and over which place the stuffed leaves one by one
Arrange between them eight or ten sour plums
Press them with a plate, then nearly cover them with water, and set the pan on the fire
When boiling, let it simmer until there is no liquid remaining
Take one out and try if the rice is soft; if not, add some more water
When soft, and each grain is separate, dish them up tastefully, and serve

title: Ydghsiz Kaddyif
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, clotted cream, and milk.
steps: Lay four or five crumpets in a rather deep baking-tin
Pour over them half a pint of milk
Sprinkle powdered sugar over
Lay a layer of clotted cream
Lay an equal number of crumpets over
Pour half a pint more milk, then sugar
Put it on a charcoal fire and let it boil for a little while
Take it off just before the cream is melted
When rather cold, dish them up carefully
Shake some powdered sugar over and serve

title: Ydghsiz Usscumru Pulalcissi
description: Prepared with mackerel, lemon, and salt.

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pint of water
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pint of water

steps: Take out the insides and the gills of seven or eight mackerel, wash them, and cut off the points of the heads and the tails
Lay some picked parsley on the bottom of a stewpan, place half of the fish over, then sprinkle a little powdered gum-mastic over, some parsley again
Lay the other half of the fish over, gum-mastic again, then parsley on the top
Add sufficient salt and pepper, and three-quarters of a pint of water
Put the pan on a charcoal fire, and let simmer gently for twenty minutes or so
Dish it up, squeeze half or the whole of a lemon over, and serve

title: Ydissi Kaddyif
description: Prepared with pistachios or almonds, orange, and sugar.
steps: Get six or seven crumpets
Put a pound of loaf sugar into a saucepan, with two pints of water
Set it to boil until it becomes a syrup
Keep it boiling gently by the side of the fire
Beat up five or six eggs in a basin
Dip the crumpets one after the other in the eggs
Fry them a nice brown on both sides in scalded fresh butter
Throw them in the syrup
Take them out instantly and dish them up
Sprinkle between each one some pounded pistachios or almonds
Put one or two drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower in a tea-cup of water
Pour it over the crumpets
Put it in the oven or on a slow charcoal fire for five minutes or so
Then serve

title: Yhghssiz Pilaw
description: Prepared with fat, rice, and water.

ingredients.name: two measures of the liquor to one of well-washed rice
ingredients.sourceText: two measures of the liquor to one of well-washed rice

ingredients.name: two or three pieces of cinnamon
ingredients.sourceText: two or three pieces of cinnamon

steps: Put one or two fat fowls in a saucepan nearly full of water, and sufficient salt, and put it on the fire.
When boiling, skim and simmer until the meat separates from the bones.
Take it off, and pass the whole through a clean cloth or sieve by pressing and squeezing it with your hand, and cast the residue away.
Put in the saucepan two measures of the liquor to one of well-washed rice, add two or three pieces of cinnamon, and a few pieces of gum-mastic.
Set it on a charcoal fire till the liquor is absorbed.
Take it off, and place it on the hob, stir it once round with a fork, and let it remain covered for fifteen minutes or so.
Take out the pieces of cinnamon, dish up, and serve hot.

title: Yoghurt
description: Prepared with curd and milk.
steps: Put four pints of pure milk into a particularly clean stewpan
Put it on a charcoal fire and let it bubble once
Take it off and pour it into a basin
When cold enough to bear your finger in it, add two tablespoonfuls of old curd

title: Yoghurtlu-Sha Ighdm
description: Turnip slices are parboiled, floured and browned in butter, then simmered briefly in broth. A curd topping, hot butter and pepper finish the dish.
steps: Peel four or five turnips, cut them in slices about a quarter or a half an inch thick
Boil them in water with a little salt, partly tender, and let them drain
When free from water, dip them in flour, and fry them a nice brown in fresh butter
Lay them in a baking-pan or a pie-dish that will bear fire
Pour half a pint of broth (No. 1) over the turnips
Set the pan on a moderate charcoal fire, and let it simmer for eight or ten minutes
Take it off, and lay some curd over the turnips, over which sprinkle a little hot fresh butter, and a pinch of pepper, and serve hot

title: Yufkâ Bureghi
description: Prepared with broth, meat, and mutton or beef.
steps: Place two or three pounds of flour on the table-dresser, or in a pan, make a hole in the centre, put in a little salt, and sufficient water, and stir it well up with a wooden spoon
Throw a little flour over, and knead well with the hands until it forms a nice paste
Divide it into small pieces (say eight or ten), and roll them out thin, about the thickness of a sixpence, and the size of a baking-tin intended for laying them in
Bake them soft, one by one, on a hot stove or a baking-sheet, which is placed over a trevet on a wood or charcoal fire
When done nicely on both sides, beat up two or three eggs in a basin, with a teacup of broth
Grease the baking-tin with fresh butter, and lay in half the pieces of paste one over the other, sprinkling some of the beaten-up egg, and fresh butter between each one with a quill or a paste-brush
Lay some fried minced meat all over, half an inch thick, which is prepared from raw mutton or beef, and then cover it with the remaining pieces of paste, as above
Egg and butter over, place it in the oven until nicely browned on both sides
When done, cut it in diamonds, or any other shape, dish up, and serve hot

title: Ankerias-keitto (Eel Soup)
description: A soup made with eel, meat or fish stock, and white wine.

ingredients.name: 4 quarts of meat or fish stock
ingredients.sourceText: 4 quarts of meat or fish stock

steps: Skin the eels, clean and cut them into one inch pieces.
Cook them in 1 quart of fish stock mixed with 3 tablespoonfuls of lemon juice, bay leaf and pepper, being careful not to break the pieces.
Leave the fish in the same liquor until next day.
Strain the bouillon and put to boil with the vegetables cut into cubes.
Add peas, cauliflower and asparagus a little later.
Cook the peeled pears in a small quantity of water with lemon juice, white wine, a piece of cinnamon and a few cloves until tender.
If the pears are too large, cut them lengthwise into slices.
Thicken the soup with butter and flour.
Put into it the eels, pears with their own liquor, and the strained tomato liquor.
Whip the yolks and pour the soup gently into it.
Cream may be used with the soup if wanted.

title: Annan Kakku (Annie Cake)

Serve with any kind of salad.
